messages:
devon: heads-up — ran a quick perf sweep on the MQA/GQA path after the kv-layout-v2 rollout. seeing a 12-18% p99 latency bump for seq_len >= 768 on A100s. rolling back the layout fixes the bump. logs and numbers below.

ana: ugh. do you have a minimal repro? is it consistently at seq_len boundary or noisy?

devon: repro is pretty consistent. microbench: `./bench --model=redwood-7b --batch=4 --seq=512/768/1024`
```
512: p50 12ms p95 34ms p99 48ms
768: p50 18ms p95 62ms p99 89ms  <-- jump
1024: p50 22ms p95 80ms p99 112ms
```

pranav: pinging the kernel selector logs — looks like at 768 we switch from the fused-paged-attn kernel to fallback-stream due to a heuristics score shift. flamegraph: https://perf.internal/flame/3459 (short link)

maria: can you paste the selector decision payload? curious which metric dropped (mem, reg pressure, or expected throughput).

devon: here's the snippet from selector (sanitized):
```
candidate_scores: [ {name: "gqa_paged_v1", score: 0.79}, {name: "mqa_fused", score: 0.65}, {name: "fallback_stream", score: 0.81} ]
chosen: fallback_stream
reason: kv_fragmentation_estimate + block_mismatch_penalty
```

ana: that +block_mismatch_penalty sounds new from the v2 kv layout estimator. might be overpenalizing interleaved shards.

perf-bot: :warning: Regression alert — infra/perf: p99 increased by 15% for endpoint /generate under commit 0x3af4b. Detect window: last 30m.

pranav: looking at GPU counters — `ld_gs` and `cache_miss` spike when the selector chooses fallback_stream. The fallback path reserializes KV pages causing extra memcopy.

maria: hypothesis: autotuner uses a static block size penalty that doesn't account for MQA lane compactness. For MQA when lanes are packed the penalty should be reduced.

devon: quick experiment idea: lower block_mismatch_penalty by 0.5 for the MQA family and re-run 768/1024 sweep in canary. I can spin canaries if infra signs off.

infra-bot: canary rollout queued: service=runtime-gpu, shard=canary-9, commit=0x3af4b, traffic=2%. started at 3459000100.

ana: also try increasing the block size probe set: add candidate block_size=128 and 256 to selector for the next autotune round. sometimes the selector misses better-aligned kernels because the probe grid was too coarse.

pranav: added probe flags locally: `--probe-blocks 64,128,256 --probe-epochs 20`. early numbers look promising: with block_size=128, gqa_paged score jumps to 0.86 and chosen kernel changes back to fused-paged-attn.

maria: nice. If this holds, we should change autotuner policy: prefer kernel latency over memory-frag penalty for seq_len in [512,1024] when model=Mx* and mqa_enabled. I'll draft the config change.

devon: after 10m canary: p99 down to baseline at 768. infra-bot shows canary healthy.

infra-bot: canary success: traffic=2% healthy=100% duration=10m. ready for ramp.

perf-bot: :white_check_mark: Regression resolved in canary: p99 back within 2% of baseline.

ana: follow-up action items: (1) add block_size probes 128/256 to default probe grid, (2) tweak autotuner policy to weigh latency higher for seq_len>=512 with mqa, (3) add a unit test to ensure block_mismatch_penalty is clipped to [0,0.5] for MQA models.

devon: will open the PR with numbers and a short perf note. thanks all.

pranav: TL;DR: kv-layout-v2 exposed an interaction where the fragmentation estimator overpenalized packed MQA lanes, causing selector to choose a higher-latency fallback kernel at mid-high seq lengths. fix is: widen probe grid + reduce penalty for MQA.

maria: adding to weekly todo for autotune: run a sweep across arch families (A100, H100, L40) and confirm the penalty tweak doesn't regress other hw.

devon: i'll run the arch sweep tomorrow and post results. closing thread for now, will update with PR link. :thumbsup:
